$$

$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$

$$

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-2\right)}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(1\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2}+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\left(1\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2} + \frac{3}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

["ea1b21db-b725-5c95-9dfd-e31f17ca067b" :question/id #uuid "ea1b21db-b725-5c95-9dfd-e31f17ca067b"] ["ea1b21db-b725-5c95-9dfd-e31f17ca067b" :question/problem "Find the equation of the normal line to the curve $y=2 x^{2} + x$ at $\left(2,10\right)$.

Give exact values of $a$ and $b$ in $y=ax+b$.

$a=$ {{slope}}

$b=$ {{intercept}}"] ["ea1b21db-b725-5c95-9dfd-e31f17ca067b" :question/worked-solution "Let $f(x)=2 x^{2} + x$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=4 x + 1
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=4 \left(2\right) + 1=9
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(9\right)}=- \frac{1}{9}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(10\right)&=- \frac{1}{9}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=- \frac{x}{9}+\left(\frac{2}{9}\right)+\left(10\right)\\
y&=\frac{92}{9} - \frac{x}{9}
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=- \frac{1}{9}$ and $b=\frac{92}{9}$."] ["ea1b21db-b725-5c95-9dfd-e31f17ca067b" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] ["ea1b21db-b725-5c95-9dfd-e31f17ca067b" :question/answer-fields "754662c5-3a1e-5018-8466-8be99aef7960"] ["ea1b21db-b725-5c95-9dfd-e31f17ca067b" :question/answer-fields "acc4aae5-f289-5b65-895e-552c65646dc6"] [17592186092240 :knowledge-point/questions "ea1b21db-b725-5c95-9dfd-e31f17ca067b"]] "retractions" []}
